official_tasks.task: Build an agentic loop that keeps iterating while the stop reason signals a tool request and ends when the model signals it is done, feeding tool results back each turn.
Use SDK hooks to normalize tool results before the model sees them and to intercept outgoing tool calls that violate business rules, redirecting to an alternative workflow.
Manage session state by resuming named sessions, forking from a shared baseline, and deciding between resume and a fresh session seeded with a summary when tool results are stale.
Write tool descriptions and boundaries (inputs, examples, edge cases, when-not-to-use) that disambiguate similar tools, and rename or split overlapping tools.
Return structured MCP tool errors that distinguish transient, validation, business and permission failures with retryability metadata, and separate access failures from valid empty results.
Give each agent a scoped tool set, avoid tool overload, and use tool_choice (auto, any, forced) to control whether and which tool is called.
Integrate MCP servers with Claude Code using project-scoped and user-scoped configuration, environment-variable expansion for secrets, and resources for content catalogs.
Pick the right built-in tool (Grep, Glob, Read, Write, Edit, Bash) for each job and build codebase understanding incrementally, with Read+Write as the fallback when Edit anchors are not unique.
Create team slash commands and skills with the right scope and frontmatter (forked context, tool restrictions, argument hints), and choose skills versus always-loaded CLAUDE.md.
Enforce schema-compliant output via tool use with JSON schemas, choose the right tool_choice mode, and design nullable fields and enum escape values to prevent fabrication.
Preserve critical facts in long interactions by keeping a persistent case-facts block, trimming verbose tool output, and ordering inputs to counter lost-in-the-middle effects.
Assess an agent or tool configuration for capability bloat and excess permissions.
Choose the integration mechanism (MCP, API/CLI, agent-to-agent) for a situation.
Monitor system performance with logging and observability tooling.
Configure Claude tools and environments such as Claude Code for teams.
Improve developer workflows with AI-assisted tooling.
Apply common agent patterns (tool-use loops, subagents, memory, context management) and agentic frameworks such as Strands, LangGraph and PydanticAI.
Use Claude API mechanics: messages, tools, streaming, vision, thinking, caching, third-party vendor access, batch use and the realtime-vs-batch tradeoff.
Control context with window management, drift and bloat prevention (tool-output pruning, compaction) and isolation via subagents or multi-step workflows.
Implement tools well: function calling, tool descriptions, error handling, dispatch in an agentic harness, client-side vs server-side tools, approval patterns and tool set construction.
Develop MCP servers: author, deploy and integrate them, exposing resources, tools and prompts over stdio or sockets.
Weigh built-in tools, custom tools, Skills and MCPs to choose the right extension mechanism.

docs_facts.fact: Project-scope MCP config at the repo root, key mcpServers. Entry fields: type (http, stdio, sse, ws, streamable-http alias), url/headers (remote), command/args/env (stdio), timeout, oauth, headersHelper. An entry with url but no type is rejected; no type means stdio. Env expansion ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} works in command, args, env, url, headers. Scopes: local (default, in ~/.claude.json), project (.mcp.json, needs approval), user; precedence local, project, user, plugin, claude.ai connectors with no field merging.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: sse transport is deprecated in favour of http; Claude Code tries HTTP then falls back to SSE (v2.1.265+).

docs_facts.fact: Three routes: static --header/-H on claude mcp add (or headers in .mcp.json), OAuth 2.0 via /mcp or claude mcp login (with --callback-port, oauth.scopes), and headersHelper, a command printing a JSON object of string headers (10-second timeout, runs per connection, no caching, re-run once after 401/403). ANTHROPIC_API_KEY-style credential variables are not expanded in remote url/headers. Tool names follow mcp__<server>__<tool>; plugin servers use mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>.

Beta feature that lets the Messages API connect to remote MCP servers without a client. Requires beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; the 2025-04-04 version is deprecated. Config has two parts: mcp_servers (type url, url, name, authorization_token) and an mcp_toolset entry in tools referencing it (allowlist/denylist via default_config and configs, defer_loading settable there). Only MCP tool calls are supported; server must be publicly reachable over HTTP (Streamable HTTP or SSE); local stdio cannot connect. Response blocks: mcp_tool_use, mcp_tool_result. Not ZDR eligible.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Old mcp-client-2025-04-04 shape (allowed_tools inside mcp_servers) is deprecated.

docs_facts.fact: Client tools (your own, plus bash/text_editor/memory/computer use) run in your app: Claude returns stop_reason tool_use with tool_use blocks, you reply with a tool_result block carrying the matching tool_use_id. Server tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution, tool_search) run on Anthropic's side. A custom tool is name, description, input_schema; strict: true guarantees schema-valid inputs. Tool definitions and tool blocks all count as input tokens, plus a per-model tool-use system prompt overhead (e.g. 286 tokens on Opus 5.5 with auto/none).

Request field controlling tool calling. Default {type: auto} lets Claude decide; values auto, none, any and tool appear in the docs (the pricing table keys on auto/none versus any/tool). auto accepts disable_parallel_tool_use: true to cap Claude at one tool call per turn. Exact semantics of any and tool and their interaction with thinking: not verified (define-tools page not fetched).

The tool value is listed as a tool_choice option (it, like any, costs more tool-use system-prompt tokens than auto/none). That it forces one named tool is not stated on the fetched page: not verified.
Default. Claude decides per turn whether to call a tool or answer directly. Can be steered with system-prompt wording; combine with disable_parallel_tool_use: true for at most one tool call per turn.

Seven values: end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn (server-tool loop hit its default 10-iteration limit; resend the assistant content to continue), refusal (HTTP 200, read stop_details, can retry on a fallback model), model_context_window_exceeded (response filled the context window; treat as truncated). A client tool_use never yields pause_turn.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: refusal and model_context_window_exceeded are newer values; older lists name only the first four.

docs_facts.fact: Request parameter capping output tokens; hitting it ends the response with stop_reason max_tokens, so raise it or continue the response. Sync output max is 128K tokens on the current models; Batches API can reach 300k with beta header output-300k-2026-03-24. Each batched request needs max_tokens of at least 1.

Server-side tool letting Claude discover tools on demand. Two variants: tool_search_tool_regex_20251119 (Claude writes Python regex, 200-char cap) and tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119 (natural language, 500-char cap). Put the full definition of every tool in tools; mark the ones to hide with defer_loading: true; at least one tool (not the search tool) must stay non-deferred, else 400. Up to 10,000 deferred tools; 5 results by default (limit 1-10,000). Preserves prompt caching; a deferred tool cannot carry cache_control. Not metered separately.

Blocks of type tool_reference returned inside the search result pointing at discovered tools by tool_name; the API expands them to full definitions server-side. Custom client-side search can also return tool_reference blocks inside a normal tool_result, and each must have a matching definition in top-level tools. Never return a tool_result for a srvtoolu_ id.
The overview shows tool_result content as a plain string or content blocks. A specific recommendation about JSON-encoding tool results: not verified.

The stop-reason page says a refusal can be retried on a fallback model and links a refusals-and-fallback page (not fetched). Claude Code separately has --fallback-model / fallbackModel for overloaded or retired models. What 'server-side fallback' specifically denotes: not verified.
Prompting best-practices page linked from models overview but not fetched: not verified.
No page fetched that defines a 'system prompt policy' feature: not verified. (Facts on system prompt flags such as --system-prompt and --append-system-prompt are in the headless/CLI entries.)
